title: Kernel autoselect: tune H100 heuristics by sequence-length buckets
author: Yuki Sato
description:
Context: As part of the hardware tuning profiles pack, we want predictable and measurable H100 behavior across a wide mix of prompt/response lengths. Our current kernel selection logic is too coarse (mostly based on “model family + attention impl availability”), which leaves meaningful perf on the table for short-prefill / mid-context / long-context buckets, and occasionally picks kernels that are stable but suboptimal for certain seq-len distributions.

What this PR does: Updates the H100 kernel auto-selection heuristics to bucket by effective prefill seq length and decode context length, and to select kernels accordingly. The intent is not to introduce new kernels; it’s to improve routing among existing implementations and to make the choice more robust under mixed workloads (including streaming).

Heuristic changes (H100 only): 1) Add seq-len buckets for prefill: S (<=512), M (513–2048), L (2049–8192), XL (>8192). 2) Add a separate decode-context bucket (ctx <=4096 vs >4096) to avoid the “one-size-fits-all” pick under long-running chats. 3) Prefer FA2 persistent kernels for S/M buckets when head_dim and layout are compatible; prefer FA2 split-k for L when batch is high; prefer paged-attn path for XL or when KV is paged due to cache budgeting. 4) Add explicit guardrails to avoid selecting the “aggressive” kernels when streaming + small batch + tight p95 SLO (these cases showed instability in earlier runs). 5) When detection is ambiguous (MIG partitions, vendor SKU string variants), fall back to the prior stable choice and emit a selection_reason metric tag.

Performance summary (microbench + perf-canary): Microbench (runtime/bench/h100_kernel_sweep) indicates net gains in tokens/sec primarily in S/M buckets, with neutral-to-slight improvements in L and no regressions in XL (where we usually end up in paged-attn anyway). Perf-canary job: https://perf-canary.redwood-inference.net/jobs/rc-145982 (H100 SXM, us-east) and https://perf-canary.redwood-inference.net/jobs/rc-146104 (H100 PCIe, us-west). Aggregate deltas vs main (median across matrix): S (<=512): +6–9% decode tok/s, p95 latency -2–4% at concurrency 16; M (513–2048): +4–7% decode tok/s, p95 latency ~flat; L (2049–8192): +0–3% tok/s, p95 latency +0–1% (within gate); XL (>8192): ~flat (within noise).

Correctness/stability: No changes to numerics expected; we’re only changing kernel selection. Added tests to ensure bucket boundaries behave as expected and to keep the fallback path intact. Also added log/metrics breadcrumbs so oncall can see (a) selected kernel impl, (b) seq bucket, (c) why we avoided a faster kernel.

Rollout plan: This is intended to be consumed by the H100 tuned profile, but it is safe as a standalone change. We will stage behind the existing runtime knob `runtime.kernel_autoselect.h100_seq_bucket_enable` defaulting ON for H100 in hosted canary pools only, and keep the ability to override OFF per pool if we see tail latency regressions.

Links: Linear ENG-4824, ENG-4821. Related PRs: PR #22003 (H100 scheduler presets), PR #21991 (profile selection logic). Microbench notes: internal bench artifact “h100-kernel-sweep-2025-12-09” (Benchmark Lab run ID bl-77219).
commits: runtime/kernels: add H100 seq-len bucket helper and enums
runtime/kernels: update autoselect to choose FA2 persistent vs split-k by bucket
runtime/kernels: add guardrails for streaming + low batch and long ctx
runtime/tests: add bucket boundary tests and fallback coverage

review_conversation:
Grace Kim: Can you clarify why the cutoff for S/M is 512/2048? We’ve seen some models behave differently around 1k.
Yuki Sato: Cutoffs are based on the sweep where FA2 persistent wins pretty consistently <=512. Between 513–2048 the win is still there but smaller; beyond 2k split-k tends to catch up at higher conc. I added a note in code and the bench script prints the crossover points for head_dim=128/64 so we can revisit.

Sofia Ivanova: Any risk that the new selection changes tail latency under streaming? Scheduler already has fairness toggles, but I’d like to avoid compounding.
Yuki Sato: Added an explicit guardrail: if streaming && batch<4 && target_p95_ms is set (SLO mode), we keep the previous “stable” kernel. Also emitting selection_reason so we can correlate in dashboards.

Rina Kobayashi: Please link the perf-canary job IDs and include the exact workload rows where you saw the largest gains.
Yuki Sato: Added links in PR description + attached the two summary artifacts. Biggest gains are in rows: chat_short_prefill_high_conc and summarize_1k_to_2k_prefill (both non-streaming).

Hiro Tanaka: Bucket XL (>8192) defaulting to paged-attn makes sense, but can you ensure we don’t pick it for 8193 when KV paging isn’t enabled? That could be a perf cliff.
Yuki Sato: Good catch. Updated to require kv_cache_mode==PAGED for the paged-attn preference; otherwise we use FA2 split-k for XL as long as memory headroom is sufficient, and we log if we override due to kv budget.

Kira Volkov: Metrics naming: please prefix with runtime_kernel_ and make bucket labels consistent with the dashboard panels.
Yuki Sato: Done. Renamed `kernel_autoselect_bucket` -> `runtime_kernel_autoselect_seq_bucket` and aligned labels to {S,M,L,XL}.

Aisha Bello: Perf gates look OK. Please add a note on expected variance; otherwise we’ll get noisy alerts when the buckets shift the mix.
Yuki Sato: Added a short note to the perf-canary README and linked it in the description. Also tagged the metric so we can segment by selected kernel.
release_notes: H100 only: improved kernel auto-selection by sequence-length buckets; adds selection metrics and guardrails to avoid streaming tail-latency regressions.
